content:
t8 is yours and it is ready now. Please pick it up with claim_task and work it before anything else.

Context so you do not have to re-derive it: your t1 floor work is good, I verified FLOOR_Y = -0.42, TRAY_DWELL = 0.9, the mouth-only tray and the chute reading G.Sim.TOP.dropZ all landed correctly, and the payout mouth reads properly as a slot in the cabinet face. This is one follow-up defect I found by zooming into your own screenshot.

The defect: a coin that has come to rest on the room floor renders as a half-moon, because the floor plane cuts through the disc. Two causes, both in the fall-mesh sync in render.js:
1. `fm2.coin.rotation.set(fc.fax * 0.4, ...)` is recomputed from fc.fax EVERY frame, so the `rotation.x *= 0.75` "settle flat" damping can never converge — it just holds the coin at 75% of its tumble, about -44 degrees. It is standing on its edge.
2. The resting height is a flat constant `+0.007` (half-thickness of a FLAT coin), but a coin tilted 44 degrees needs up to COIN_R = 0.036 of clearance, so about 29 mm of it is underground.

Probe values I measured on the two resting coins: fax -2.556 / faz -4.4964 and fax -7.006 / faz 1.6026, both at fy -0.42.

Fix: when resting, do not re-derive rotation from fax at all — give it a truly flat pose (x and z at 0, spin only about Y), and lift it by G.Sim.COIN_R * 0.21 instead of the magic 0.007. Same class of fix for the resting prop branch, which currently keeps its tilt and clips the floor too. Keep the airborne tumble untouched.

Also please tighten FIT_POINTS while you are in there — the desktop frame still has that dead floor band you flagged, and I agree it is too much.

Scope stays render.js only. sim.js is off limits (its constants are correct, this is purely a pose/height problem) and main.js is being edited by glue right now.
